results.name: digit_run_nonmatch_rate
results.description: Yes-rate, over all trials of sets with >=3 examples that all share one final digit, for targets that do NOT have that final digit; observed < null means people treat a run of same-final-digit examples as a strict rule and reject non-matching targets more than the model predicts, observed > null means more lenient than predicted.

results.name: multiple_of_five_set_contrast
results.description: In sets with >=2 examples that are all multiples of 5, mean yes-rate for targets that are multiples of 5 minus mean yes-rate for targets that are not; observed > null means people extend a multiples-of-5 rule more sharply than the model's final-digit/magnitude similarity predicts, observed < null means the model over-generalizes along it.

results.name: set_level_yes_rate_sd
results.description: SD across sets (with >=3 distinct targets) of each set's mean yes-rate; observed > null means people's overall willingness to say yes varies by set more than the model's single similarity-to-response mapping produces (set-specific rule breadth), observed < null means less.
results.code:
# name: set_level_yes_rate_sd
# description: SD across sets (with >=3 distinct targets) of each set's mean yes-rate; observed > null means people's overall willingness to say yes varies by set more than the model's single similarity-to-response mapping produces (set-specific rule breadth), observed < null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    g = df.groupby("number_set")
    m = g["rating"].mean()
    nt = g["target"].nunique()
    v = m[nt >= 3].values.astype(float)
    return float(np.std(v)) if len(v) > 1 else 0.0

results.name: power_of_two_contrast
results.description: In sets whose examples are all powers of 2, mean yes-rate for power-of-2 targets minus mean yes-rate for other targets (difference of two trial-level means; 0 if a group is empty); observed > null means people use a powers-of-2 rule more sharply than the model's magnitude/digit/parity/shared-factor similarity predicts, observed < null means less.

results.name: trial_index_drift
results.description: Pearson correlation between trial_index and the yes response across all trials; observed != null (null ~0, the model has no time dependence) means people drift toward saying yes (positive) or no (negative) over the session.

results.name: within_set_item_sd
results.description: Average, over sets tested with >=9 distinct targets, of the SD across that set's targets of per-target yes-rate; observed > null means people discriminate among targets of the same set more sharply than the model, observed < null means people's responses within a set are flatter (more uniform) than the model's graded similarity predicts.
results.code:
# name: within_set_item_sd
# description: Average, over sets tested with >=9 distinct targets, of the SD across that set's targets of per-target yes-rate; observed > null means people discriminate among targets of the same set more sharply than the model, observed < null means people's responses within a set are flatter (more uniform) than the model's graded similarity predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    it = df.groupby(["number_set", "target"])["rating"].mean().reset_index()
    g = it.groupby("number_set")["rating"]
    sd = g.std(ddof=0)
    n = g.size()
    v = sd[n >= 9].values.astype(float)
    return float(np.mean(v)) if len(v) else 0.0

results.name: set_size_slope
results.description: OLS slope of trial-level yes response on the number of examples in the set (1-4); observed < null means more examples make people more conservative (size-principle tightening) than the model's summed similarity allows, observed > null means more examples make people more liberal than predicted.

results.name: common_factor_nodigit_contrast
results.description: Among targets matching no example's final digit and not equal to an example (sets with >=2 examples), yes-rate for targets sharing a divisor >1 with EVERY example minus yes-rate for targets coprime with at least one example; observed < null means the model's coprime penalty over-credits shared factors (people don't use shared divisibility that much), observed > null means people reward shared factors more than modelled.
